tutorial.introduce-curb-ramp: This arrow points to a curb ramp (or "curb cut") — it lets wheelchair users move between the sidewalk and the street. Let's label it!
tutorial.select-label-type-1: Click this "Curb Ramp" button to label the curb ramp.
tutorial.label-attribute-1: Good! Now click the curb ramp beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label it.
tutorial.rate-severity-1: Now rate the curb ramp's quality. The slope and tactile warning strip are good, but the ramp points into traffic so click {{rating}}.
tutorial.redo-rate-attribute-1: Uh-oh — this ramp is decent, but pointing into traffic makes it just OK. Click {{rating}}.
tutorial.tag-attribute-1: Good! It's also helpful to add tags, so click the {{tag}} tag to capture more detail.
tutorial.redo-tag-attribute-1: Hmm — pointing into traffic is this ramp's only issue. Add just the {{tag}} tag.
tutorial.select-label-type-2: Now let's label the painted crosswalk. Click the "Marked Crosswalk" button.
tutorial.label-attribute-2: Great! Now click beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label the crosswalk.
tutorial.adjust-heading-angle-1: Great! Let’s adjust the view to look at another corner of the intersection. Grab and drag the Street View image to look left.
tutorial.zoom-in: Hmm, the corner is too far away to see clearly. Click the “Zoom In” button — or press Z. Most controls have keyboard shortcuts like this.
tutorial.select-label-type-3: Great! Now you’ve found another curb ramp. Let’s label it! Click the “Curb Ramp” button like before.
tutorial.label-attribute-3: Now click the curb ramp beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label it.
tutorial.rate-severity-3: This ramp is positioned better than the last one, but it has no flat landing space at the top, so again click {{rating}}.
tutorial.redo-rate-attribute-3: Uh-oh — the missing landing space at the top is this ramp's only problem. Click {{rating}}.
tutorial.tag-attribute-3: Good! Now click the {{tag}} tag to record the missing landing space.
tutorial.redo-tag-attribute-3: Only one tag applies here — the ramp has a tactile warning and isn't narrow or steep. Add just the {{tag}} tag.
tutorial.select-label-type-4: Notice that there is no curb ramp at the end of this crosswalk. Click the "Missing Curb Ramp" button to label it.
tutorial.label-attribute-4: Now click beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label the missing curb ramp.
tutorial.rate-severity-4: A missing curb ramp is a serious barrier. The nearby ramp is a fallback, but it routes wheelchair users into traffic — so click {{rating1}} or {{rating2}}, using your best judgment.
tutorial.redo-rate-attribute-4: Hmm — a missing curb ramp is a real accessibility barrier, even with another ramp nearby. Click {{rating1}} or {{rating2}}.
tutorial.tag-attribute-4: Click the {{tag}} tag to record that nearby curb ramp.
tutorial.redo-tag-attribute-4: Only one tag applies here. Add just the {{tag}} tag.
tutorial.select-label-type-5: On the pole you can see a light telling pedestrians that they can cross the street. Click the "Pedestrian Signal" button to label it.
tutorial.label-attribute-5: Click beneath the flashing yellow arrow, at the base of the pole — labeling the base, not the light, gives us a more accurate location.
tutorial.zoom-out: Now let's look at the next corner. Click the “Zoom Out” button — or press Shift+Z.
tutorial.adjust-heading-angle-2: Look to the left by grabbing and dragging the Street View image.
tutorial.select-label-type-6: There seems to be a painted crosswalk here as well. First, click on the "Marked Crosswalk" button.
tutorial.label-attribute-6: Let's label it by placing your label near the center of the crosswalk. Click below the flashing arrow to add your label.
tutorial.speed-things-up: To speed up the tutorial, we've labeled these two curb ramps, this crosswalk, and this pedestrian signal for you. In real missions, spotting these is your job!
tutorial.select-label-type-7: Notice that the sidewalk suddenly ends here. Let’s label this. Click the "No Sidewalk" button to label it.
tutorial.label-attribute-7: Click on the ground where the sidewalk is missing.
tutorial.tag-attribute-7: Add the {{tag1}} and {{tag2}} tags — the sidewalk stops here, but the other side of the street has one.
tutorial.redo-tag-attribute-7: Only those two tags apply here. Add just the {{tag1}} and {{tag2}} tags.
tutorial.adjust-heading-angle-4: Awesome! Let’s finish labeling the last curb ramp in the intersection. First, grab and drag the Street View image.
tutorial.select-label-type-8: Good! Now click the "Curb Ramp" button — or just press {{key}}, much faster than mousing up to the menu.
tutorial.label-attribute-8: Click the curb ramp beneath the flashing yellow arrow to label it.
tutorial.rate-severity-8: Rate this curb ramp's quality — it's wide, has a tactile warning, and doesn't point into traffic, so click {{rating}}. You can also write notes in the description box.
tutorial.redo-rate-attribute-8: Uh-oh — this ramp is wide, has a tactile warning, and doesn't point into traffic. Click {{rating}}.
tutorial.select-label-type-9: We shouldn't forget the pedestrian signal! Click the "Pedestrian Signal" button — or press {{key}}.
tutorial.label-attribute-9: Click at the base of the pole to label this pedestrian signal.
tutorial.adjust-heading-angle-5: Great Job! We are almost done. Now let’s learn how to move. Grab and drag the Street View image.
tutorial.walk-1: Good! Now to figure out where to go next, you will follow the red line on this mini map.
tutorial.walk-2: We will also guide you via navigation messages shown in this area. You can click on them to turn or move.
tutorial.walk-3: Now let's actually move forward! You can click on the navigation message, or you can click on the arrow that points in the direction you want to move.
tutorial.walk-4: Great! You just moved down the street. Visited parts of a route are marked in green in the mini map.
tutorial.walk-5-1: Now you can look for more issues at this location. In this case, notice how there is a crosswalk with pedestrian signals but no curb ramps at either end.
tutorial.walk-5-2: Yes! I see the missing curb ramps.
tutorial.walk-6: Here are a few more examples at this corner. Let's finish up and get you onto a real mission!
tutorial.instruction-1: You can track your labels in the mini map!
tutorial.instruction-2: Finally, if you get stuck while exploring, you can use the Stuck button to move to a different location.

common.rate-crosswalk-sev-1: Now rate the crosswalk's quality. The surface is smooth and the paint isn't fading, so click {{rating}}.
common.redo-rate-crosswalk-sev-1: Uh-oh — the surface is smooth and the paint isn't fading, so this crosswalk is high quality. Click {{rating}}.

popup.both-sides-title: Please check both sides of the street
popup.both-sides-body: As you explore, remember to check both sides of the street like this:
popup.labels-disappear-body: Wondering where your labels went? After you move, you won't see them in the Street View image anymore, but you can still see them on the highlighted mini map!
popup.jump: You have been moved to a new location.
popup.jump-auto: We have automatically moved you to a new location.
popup.signup-body: Do you want to create an account to keep track of your progress?

popup.zoom-shortcuts: You can also press the <kbd>Z</kbd> key to zoom in and the <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Z</kbd> keys to zoom out.

popup.label-shortcuts-obstacle: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the Obstacle label.
popup.label-shortcuts-surface-problem: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the Surface Problem label.
popup.label-shortcuts-no-sidewalk: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the No Sidewalk label.
popup.label-shortcuts-crosswalk: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the Marked Crosswalk label.
popup.label-shortcuts-signal: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the Pedestrian Signal label.
popup.label-shortcuts-occlusion: You can also press the <kbd>{{key}}</kbd> key for selecting the Can't See the Sidewalk label.
popup.still-stuck: If you're still stuck, click the Stuck button again.
popup.stuck-skipped-street: We couldn't find a spot for you on that street, so we moved you to a new street.
popup.free-explore-start: You've been dropped near your searched address. Look around and label what you find!
popup.free-explore-start-named: You've been dropped close to {{placeName}}. Look around and label what you find!
popup.free-explore-no-imagery: There's no more street imagery in this direction. Try looking around or heading the other way.
popup.stuck-suggestion: If you can't move with the arrows, trying clicking on the navigation directions in the bottom right. Or try clicking on the Stuck button on the left.
